_comment: Frames-per-second observed on the actual V100 production host (cds2 / 100.98.2.11), extracted
from returned run artifacts. NOT part of the evaluator closure -- deliberately not in
families.json, which is a CONFIG_MEMBER whose modification would invalidate every attestation.
A row is an OBSERVED RATE of one past cell, under the conditions stated. It is evidence toward
this host's throughput for that baseline, never a promise for a future cell -- see
notes/production-host/10-resource-upper-bound-rule.md's sibling principle for VRAM, which
applies here for the same reason: this project has already lost a cell (svea s101 attempt 2,
2026-09-19) to a throughput figure measured under different conditions being trusted uncritically.
[2026-09-20] Every entry names: which run, which date, what was actually measured (frames and
elapsed wall-clock time, from the artifact), the conditions the cell ran under (card sharing,
co-tenants, loader configuration), and whether it is MEASURED (this laptop holds the raw
artifact) or DOC-QUOTED (the artifact is not on this laptop; the figure is read from a dated
note instead and marked as such -- never silently promoted to 'measured').
`per_baseline` is DERIVED, not a second source of truth: it is the minimum usable
frames_per_second among a baseline's non-flagged cells (MEASURED or DOC-QUOTED alike), because
this file's one real consumer -- sizing a wall-clock CELL_TIMEOUT -- must not be optimistic.
Taking a max or a mean would let one lucky cell size the timeout for every future one; the
svea incident is the concrete cost of trusting an optimistic figure (production-schedule.json's
9.99 fps, itself a T4-tier reference, not even a V100 one) against a slower real run. A single
usable cell trivially IS the minimum. A baseline whose only sample is FLAGGED (svea) has no
usable cell and stays null/UNMEASURED_ON_V100 -- see cells[].representativeness.

cells.elapsed_human: 35 min (approximate; the cited note gives only the round figure)
cells.measurement_basis: doc-quoted, artifact not local: notes/CURRENT-STATE-AND-RESPONSIBILITY.md:100-101 states the cell 'reached frame 9,000 in 35 minutes -- ~2.4 FPS with GPU util 0'. FLAGGED DISCREPANCY, not resolved here: naive division (9,000 frames / 2,100 s) gives ~4.29 fps, not 2.4 -- the doc's '~2.4 FPS' is presumably the training loop's own instantaneous/windowed FPS field at the moment of the last log line (matching the coordinator's own quoted format 'F: 9000 ... FPS: 2.43 ... T: 0:35:28' from an earlier session), which need not equal the cumulative average if throughput was decaying over the sample. Both numbers are recorded; frames_per_second below is the doc's own headline figure, not the naive one, because it is the number the doc bolds and the one G10/G12 reason from
cells.artifact: doc-quoted, artifact not local (notes/CURRENT-STATE-AND-RESPONSIBILITY.md:100-101); only runs/card1-20260919-204235/native-out/cells/svea-s101/effective_config.json is on this laptop (confirms RLVIGEN_PLACES_WORKERS=0, frames_requested=600000), no training.log or train.csv
cells.conditions: GPU util 0; Places365 overlay-loader workers = 0 (RLVIGEN_PLACES_WORKERS=0, the silent default at run_probe.sh:2206, confirmed in the local effective_config.json); file cache cold; host shared; host crashed uncleanly at ~21:25 MSK (unrelated to the throughput figure, which was sampled 20:42-21:17)
cells.representativeness: FLAGGED -- known-defective sample, MUST NOT be used as svea's throughput. notes/ACCOUNTABILITY.md G10 (line 463): 'The Places365 baselines' scheduled throughput is from a banned loader configuration... at 0 workers the one sample is ~2.4 FPS for svea (schedule: 9.99)'. G12 (line 465) is the prepared-not-run experiment to establish a real 0-worker rate on a warm cache, idle host, across multiple attempts -- this single 35-minute cold-cache sample under a suspected-defective configuration is exactly what G12 exists to replace, not to stand in for

idaac.source: idaac-s102 (card1-20260916-213222, measured) -- selected as the minimum of 3 usable cells

ibac_sni.rule: single usable cell (n=1, measured); AGGREGATE across procs=16, see the cell entry's note

svea.rule: EXCLUDED -- the only sample (svea-s101-attempt2) is flagged as a known-defective configuration and is not a usable measurement of this baseline's throughput
